result:
Alright, let's just let this go where it goes.

I keep thinking about how most people treat time like it's a container that needs to be filled. Calendars, to-do lists, "productive" hours. But time isn't a box; it's more like weather. Sometimes it moves straight through you. Sometimes it pools and gets stagnant. The truly weird hours are the ones where nothing is scheduled and your mind starts wandering without permission.

Take the way ideas actually arrive. Not the ones you chase, but the ones that show up while you're washing a plate or staring at a wall. They don't knock. They just appear half-formed, like someone left a strange object on your porch in the middle of the night. You either pick it up or you don't. Most of the interesting stuff in history probably started that way — some person who was supposed to be doing something else noticed an anomaly and refused to file it under "irrelevant." 

The part that fascinates me is how fragile that state is. Most systems, both personal and cultural, are designed to kill it. Schools reward quick answers over slow noticing. Work rewards output over wondering what the work is actually for. Even entertainment has gotten optimized to remove any gaps where a stray thought might grow. We're becoming specialists in consuming ready-made things and forgetting how to entertain ourselves with nothing but our own unfocused attention.

And yet the capacity never fully disappears. You can still feel it occasionally — usually when you're tired or bored or slightly lost. That's when patterns that were invisible before start suggesting themselves. Not in a dramatic "eureka" way. Just a quiet rearrangement of what's already in front of you.

I don't know if that makes the good ideas more valuable or less. Probably both. Valuable because they're rare under current conditions. Less, because they can't really be scheduled or forced, which means most of what we build around them is scaffolding rather than the thing itself.

Anyway. That's the corner of the room my mind wandered into just now.
